# beautify-opencode A skin for the [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) TUI that makes what is **already on screen** look like [btop](https://github.com/aristocratos/btop): rounded boxes with the title set into the top border, square meter bars, a gradient logo. It **adds nothing**. No new panels, gauges or widgets. It only restyles what OpenCode and your other plugins already draw, and every colour comes from your active theme. Switch themes and the skin follows.

Rendered by the plugin itself on OpenTUI, with a theme captured from a live OpenCode session (see Development).

## What it restyles - **Cards.** Bordered boxes get rounded corners and a border tinted with their own title colour. The header row moves into the top border, btop style, with the version label on the right. Clicks on the border row still reach the original header, so collapse toggles keep working. - **Sidebar sections.** The host's *Context* and *MCP* sections, and plugin sections such as Checklist-to-Goal, get boxed the same way, even though they draw no border of their own. - **Bars.** Magic-context's segmented token bar and any block-character text bar (Checklist-to-Goal, recomp progress…) are repainted as btop meter cells. - **Logo.** The home logo gets a vertical gradient built from a theme colour ramp.

Everything is matched heuristically and defensively. A node that does not match exactly is left alone, so if OpenCode or a plugin changes its layout, the result is "looks stock", never a broken screen. Disabling the plugin restores every node it touched. ## Installation Requires OpenCode 2.x (the V2 TUI). Add it to the `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ "beautify-opencode" ] } ``` With options: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "beautify-opencode", "options": { "logoHue": "blue" } } ] } ``` To run it from a local checkout, put the directory path in `package` (`"C:/path/to/beautify-opencode"`). The TUI hot-reloads the plugin when its files change. ## Options

| Option | Default | What it does | |-----------------|--------------|--------------| | `palette` | `"neon"` | `"neon"`: btop look with theme colours (box frames cycle through the theme's hues, white titles). `"btop"`: btop's exact default colours. `"theme"`: softer, frames tinted by each card's title. | | `cards` | `true` | Rounded, unified, compact card borders. | | `cardTitles` | `true` | Move each card's header into its top border. | | `boxBars` | `true` | Repaint magic-context's segmented token bar. | | `textBars` | `true` | Repaint block-character text bars as meters. | | `barStyle` | `"btop"` | `"btop"` (square cells) or `"glossy"` (a smooth pill). | | `meterGradient` | `"progress"` | `"progress"` (green ramp) or `"usage"` (green → yellow → red). | | `logo` | `true` | Gradient on the home logo. | | `logoGradient` | `"theme"` | `"theme"`, a named gradient (`gelo`, `aurora`, `lavanda`, `brasa`, `btop`), or your own stops: `["#cfefff", "#5aa9ff"]`. | | `logoHue` | `"accent"` | Theme ramp used by `logoGradient: "theme"`: `accent`, `interactive`, `blue`, `purple`, `cyan`, `green`… | | `scanMs` | `300` | Backstop scan interval on idle screens. | ## How it works OpenCode's TUI is an [OpenTUI](https://github.com/sst/opentui) renderable tree. The plugin keeps no slots of its own. It walks `renderer.root` and patches the nodes it recognises: - Style changes (border, padding, margins) are applied in a lifecycle pass that runs before each frame's layout, so the stock look never shows for a frame. - Titles and bars are painted in a post-process step after the frame is drawn. Sidebar sections keep their title row visible and get a box without a top edge; the post-process paints the top border, title included, over that row. Layout is never changed, so a section that rebuilds itself every second (as Checklist-to-Goal does) cannot make the screen jump. - Original properties are stored on each node, and `stop()` puts them back. On hot reload the newest instance wins and older ones go inert. ## Development There is no build step: `src/` is plain JavaScript. The tests render a replica of the sidebar and logo with OpenTUI and write an HTML preview. They need Bun; OpenCode's own binary can act as Bun: ```sh BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode test/preview.mjs preview.html BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode test/logo.mjs logo.html ``` The README images come from `docs/shots.mjs`, which renders these replicas with the real skin and a theme captured from a live TUI: ```sh BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode docs/shots.mjs # then screenshot docs/shots.html ``` Debug: create an empty `.debug` file next to `package.json`. The live tree and bar diagnostics are then written to `.debug-out/` every 5 seconds. ## License MIT
